title: Tor of opcycles is the tensor image-inclusion kernel
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and P a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Fix an integer a and assume that P^a is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put K = im(d^{a-1}) and let iota: K \hookrightarrow P^a be its inclusion. Then the functor N \mapsto \operatorname{Tor}_1^A(P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1}),N) [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] is naturally isomorphic to N \mapsto \ker(iota \otimes_A 1_N). The kernel functor means the kernel in the category of A-module-valued functors of the natural transformation iota \otimes_A -.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: Factor the differential through its abelian image. The opcycles projection is its cokernel. Exactness is unchanged on replacing the first map by its image inclusion, so this gives a short exact sequence with middle term P^a.

Tor symmetry identifies Tor_1(P^a,N) with Tor_1(N,P^a). Compute the latter using a projective resolution of N. Tensoring the exact short complex in degrees 2,1,0 with the flat module P^a preserves exactness, so its homology in degree 1 is zero.

Use the first-variable Tor exact sequence to obtain a boundary from Tor_1(P.opcycles a,N) into K tensor N, natural in N. Its composite with iota tensor N is zero; take its lift to the functor-category kernel.

The boundary is injective because its preceding Tor term is zero. For an element of the evaluated kernel, its image in K tensor N is killed by iota tensor N. Exactness lifts it along the boundary. The monic evaluated kernel inclusion shows that this lift is a preimage under the lifted map. Thus each component is mono and epi, hence an isomorphism. A natural transformation with isomorphic components is an isomorphism.

theorem nonempty_tor_opcycles_tensor_image_kernel_iso
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (a : ℤ) (hflat : Module.Flat A (P.X a)) :
    Nonempty ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) 1).obj (P.opcycles a) ≅
      Limits.kernel ((curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{u} A)).map
        (Abelian.image.ι (P.d (a - 1) a))))
